The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Binance uncovers wider breach in $6.3 billion exploit, targets Sunday withdrawal restart. CEO Richard Teng said hackers erased evidence and bypassed security checks. Binance plans to publish its proof of reserves Monday. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Wall Street analysts urge investors to buy crypto stocks after $6.3 billion Binance hack. Analysts at Cantor Fitzgerald, TD Cowen and Compass Point say the $6.3 billion Binance hack is unlikely to derail the crypto market's recovery. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Binance arranges $6.34 billion to cover losses from record crypto hack. Binance said it reserved its own funds to cover the $6.3 billion hack, including freezes of roughly $3 billion in stolen assets. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Here's how big bitcoin traders responded after the Binance hack hit. Your day-ahead look for Oct. 30, 2026 Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Here’s how an Ethereum upgrade helped drain part of Binance’s $6 billion loss. On Ethereum, the attacker used a 2025 upgrade built to make ordinary wallets smarter, armed with 50 signatures from Binance's own wallet. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Crypto liquidations jump to $1.57 billion as Binance hack sends bitcoin, ether lower. Bitcoin traded near $77,350 after $6.3 billion Binance hack, with crypto futures liquidations jumping to $1.57 billion. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $76,648 with a -4.88% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,225.87 with a -4.28% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

# Crypto Today: Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP tick lower amid mixed ETF flows

Crypto Today: Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP tick lower amid mixed ETF flows
John Isige

Bitcoin (BTC) is trading above $81,000 on Tuesday, aligning with a lethargic tone in the broader cryptocurrency market. The support range between $80,000-$81,000 reinforces the prevailing stability and consolidation, prompting institutional inflows. [...] Ethereum spot ETFs, on the other hand, recorded $103 million in outflows on Monday, sustaining a four-day bearish streak. Looking back, since September 29, ETH ETFs have posted only one day of inflows, totaling $25 million on October 13. [...] Institutional investors staged a comeback on Monday, with $527 million in Bitcoin spot Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs), up from roughly $82 million in outflows last Friday. Broadly, cumulative inflows stand at $57.4 billion, with net assets under management at $105 billion, according to SoSoValue data. A steady inflow pattern would cushion Bitcoin against headwinds, increasing the odds of a recovery.

items.title: Ethereum ETFs Outpace Bitcoin ETFs in 2026 Inflows
items.description:
Ethereum ETF inflows into U.S. spot Ethereum (CRYPTO:ETH) funds reached approximately $1.5 billion, surpassing the $985 million that spot Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) ETFs brought in. This data, sourced from SoSoValue, shows daily crypto ETF inflows and outflows. Spot ETFs directly hold the coins, so their share prices rise and fall with the cryptocurrency's market value. [...] Ethereum ETFs pulled in $1.5B in 2026 inflows, topping Bitcoin's $985M, yet Bitcoin ETFs still hold $109B in total assets, a figure roughly six times greater.
 Bitcoin ETFs staged a massive Q3 recovery, attracting $6.3 billion after $5 billion in net outflows during the first half of 2026.
 Ethereum is outpacing Bitcoin's inflow rate by $525M annually, but closing Bitcoin's $44B cumulative lead would still take over 80 years. [...] Over the years, Bitcoin ETFs have collected a staggering $57.6 billion in net inflows since their inception, whereas Ethereum funds have garnered $13.8 billion. Bitcoin ETFs began trading in January 2024—about six months before Ethereum funds, which debuted in July 2024.

At the current inflow rate, Ethereum funds are outpacing Bitcoin funds by about $525 million annually. However, it would take more than 80 years to close the existing $44 billion gap in total inflows.

items.title: Cryptocurrency regulation: U.S. laws and global developments
items.description: Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it's an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress has moved toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, while broader market structure legislation known as the CLARITY Act advanced in Congress in 2026 but has yet to become law. [...] United Kingdom. The U.K. began regulating cryptocurrency in 2020. In October 2023, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) introduced stricter rules on crypto advertising. The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 also expanded oversight of stablecoins. A broader regulatory framework was approved in 2026 and is scheduled to take effect in October 2027, bringing activities including crypto trading, custody, staking, and stablecoin issuance under FCA oversight. [...] Cryptocurrency regulation in the United States has historically been fragmented, with federal agencies applying different interpretations based on the nature and use of each asset. That splintered approach began to change in 2025, when Congress established a federal framework for stablecoins. Broader regulation of digital asset markets remains unsettled, although Congress and federal regulators have taken steps toward clarifying which assets and activities fall under securities or commodities

items.description:
Title: The Macro Playbook: How Rates, Inflation, the Dollar and Geopolitics Move Markets — TradeAI Best - Financial Intelligence
# The Macro Playbook: How Rates, Inflation, the Dollar and Geopolitics Move Markets. *Every trading day, four forces set the weather for every asset you own: interest rates, inflation, the U.S. dollar, and geopolitics. Most investors react to them one headline at a time. This playbook explains how the machine actually works — how a Fed decision travels through bond yields into stock valuations, why the dollar acts like the world’s margin call, and why most geopolitical shocks fade while a few change everything. global macro analysis · how interest rates move markets · dollar and the stock market · geopolitics and oil prices · inflation and stocks · macro regimes explained. Strip away the jargon and every macro debate reduces to one sentence: **asset prices are a claim on future cash flows, discounted by interest rates, adjusted for risk.** Growth expectations set the cash flows. Inflation, the dollar, and geopolitics constantly re-price both. When you see a violent market day, the productive question is never “what happened?” — it’s “which of the three inputs just changed: expected cash flows, the discount rate, or the risk premium?” The June 2026 crypto unwind we documented in our Bitcoin worst-month post-mortem was a textbook case: a liquidity drain (the SpaceX IPO) plus a hawkish repricing of the discount rate produced a 20% monthly decline without a single piece of bad news about Bitcoin itself. Warren Buffett’s line — “interest rates are to asset prices what gravity is to matter” — is not a metaphor, it’s arithmetic. This is why “long-duration” assets (unprofitable tech, 30-year bonds, crypto) are the most rate-sensitive things you can own: more of their value lives far in the future, where the discounting compounds hardest. The Fed raised its policy rate from near zero to 4.25–4.50% in a single year — the fastest tightening since the early 1980s — and the 10-year Treasury yield repriced from 1.51% to 3.88%. First, watch the **10-year yield**, not just the Fed’s headline rate — equities discount off the long end, and the long end moves on expectations, often months before the Fed does anything.

On Polymarket, geopolitical escalation markets (Iran, Israel, military action) and crypto price threshold markets (Bitcoin above $X) are traded by different communities. When a geopolitical shock hits, the geo markets reprice within minutes but crypto threshold markets often take hours to adjust. This skill detects that lag and trades it.

    Geopolitical escalation: Iran, Israel, military, war, attack, strike, missile, escalation
    Geopolitical de-escalation: ceasefire, peace, truce, negotiation (inverted for heat calc)
    Crypto threshold: Bitcoin above $X, Bitcoin price, BTC above, ETH above
3. Compute geo\_heat: weighted average of escalation market probabilities (de-escalation inverted)

items.title: Monero to Ethereum Swap Guide / Grok / X
items.description:
The quoted rate for a monero to ethereum swap is derived from major cryptocurrency markets. It typically includes a service spread or fee, commonly ranging from 0.5 % to 2 % depending on volume, liquidity, and the platform’s pricing model. Larger swaps may receive slightly better rates because fixed operational costs are amortized. Rates can move quickly; Monero and Ethereum prices are both influenced by overall crypto market sentiment, so the final amount received may differ from the initial [...] Before initiating any monero to ethereum swap, confirm the current market rate on multiple independent sources, estimate total fees, and ensure the destination wallet is ready and backed up. Keep records of transaction IDs from both networks in case support is needed. Because cryptocurrency markets operate continuously and prices can shift rapidly, timing and preparation matter more than attempting to optimize every basis point of the rate. [...] Rate volatility: With floating-rate swaps, the value of XMR relative to ETH can change between the moment of quoting and the moment the deposit is locked. Fixed-rate options mitigate this risk for a limited window.
 Service downtime or liquidity shortages: Platforms may temporarily pause pairs if liquidity is thin or maintenance is required. Checking recent user reports or status pages helps.
